source.title: Exploring Instruction Data Quality for Explainable Image Quality Assessment
source.authors: Yunhao Li; Sijing Wu; Jun Jia; Kang Fu; Qi Jia; Yucheng Zhu; Wei Sun; Guangtao Zhai

record.file_problem: None noted; the full paper text, including supplementary material, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It measures downstream benchmark performance across instruction-data ratios and model sizes, bearing on downstream predictability, but does not measure held-out pretraining loss or fit the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The paper reports Q-Bench overall accuracy after fine-tuning with different Q-Instruct data ratios, and accuracy for InternVL3 models of different sizes. These are relevant to V6. The Q-Selector comparisons, ablations, and fixed-ratio AesBench results do not test the listed scaling-law versions and are omitted.
record.test_reason: This is a weak test, limited to V6. The paper is about selecting instruction data for explainable image-quality assessment, not about scaling. Its only result on a claim version is downstream Q-Bench accuracy for three InternVL3 sizes (2B, 8B, 38B), before and after fine-tuning. These are off-the-shelf models, so size is not varied under control. The fine-tuning data-ratio sweep varies instruction-tuning data for one fixed pretrained model and measures accuracy. That is not the pretraining scale or loss V6 names, nor the loss-based power-law form V5 names, so it goes under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly right. The authors conclude that a randomly selected subset of instruction data at a suitable ratio can beat full-data fine-tuning for explainable IQA, which indicates redundancy. Their Q-Selector reaches 102.1% (Q-Bench) and 103.7% (AesBench) of full-data performance with 10% of the data, at about one eighth of the fine-tuning cost.
record.recipe_differences: Uses supervised fine-tuning on selected instruction data and benchmark accuracy, rather than pretraining sweeps measured by held-out cross-entropy or fixed-compute allocation.
record.method_sensitivity: Downstream accuracy varies with Q-Instruct fine-tuning data ratio; reported baseline accuracy also differs across InternVL3 model sizes.

fits_no_version.finding: For InternVL3-8B-Instruct fine-tuned on Q-Instruct with LoRA for one epoch, Q-Bench accuracy is non-monotonic in the fraction of instruction data used. The best score (78.93) is at 20%, while 100% gives 77.73 and the pretrained model 75.59. On AesBench, random 10% (59.44) beats full data (58.89).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream accuracy after instruction fine-tuning does not increase monotonically with instruction-data quantity for strong pretrained multimodal models; redundant data shows diminishing or negative returns.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the accuracy results. The paper supplies only a limited model-size comparison and does not fit or test a power-law relationship.
record.rows_left_out: Omitted Q-Bench subcategory scores in Table 1 because the overall accuracy rows capture the data-ratio comparison; omitted fixed-ratio data-selection comparisons, ablations, and AesBench results because they do not test the listed scaling-law versions.

untested.parts: No held-out pretraining loss versus parameters, tokens or compute.
No fitted laws and no extrapolation.
No shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
No loss curves or power-law fits in the fine-tuning or multimodal regime.
Downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss; controlled scale sweeps; any fitted or predictive relation; tasks beyond Q-Bench.
No fitted exponents or fitting choices.

missing.what: Post-fine-tuning Q-Bench accuracy across model sizes: 2B with 100% data 73.91, 38B with 100% data 79.06, 8B with full data 77.73. This gives a second size comparison after fine-tuning.

record.verdict_notes: The paper is not a scaling-law study; it mentions the 'data scaling law' only as motivation. The V6 evidence comes from three heterogeneous released models, so it is weak. The data-ratio sweep is the paper's main scale-related result, but it concerns fine-tuning data quantity and accuracy, not the pretraining loss or power-law form the versions name. No uncertainty estimates are reported, and each condition appears to be a single run.

versions.untested_parts: Held-out pretraining cross-entropy versus parameter count, tokens, or compute.
No small-run power-law fits or predictions of much larger runs.
No fixed-compute comparison or compute-optimal parameter/token allocation.
No controlled comparison of architecture shape at fixed parameter count.
The study evaluates image-quality tasks and fine-tuning data quantities, but does not test whether the same power-law form holds across modalities or training regimes.

Tests Q-Bench accuracy across Q-Instruct fine-tuning data ratios and reports baseline accuracy at three model sizes; does not test downstream performance as a function of pretraining loss or across a broad range of downstream tasks.
No fitted exponents or compute-optimal allocation estimates are compared across fitting choices.

relationships.condition: Off-the-shelf InternVL3 models (2B, 8B, 38B), Q-Bench overall accuracy, before fine-tuning
relationships.reason: Accuracy rises with size: 70.37, 75.59 and 76.85 (r10–r12). The fine-tuned 2B and 38B models also rank by size (73.91 at 2B, 79.06 at 38B, Table 8, from the text). The trend is monotone but uncontrolled across only three points, so it shows no predictable law.
relationships.display_finding: Untuned accuracy rose from 70.37 to 75.59 to 76.85 across 2B, 8B and 38B, while fine-tuned accuracy rose from 73.91 at 2B to 79.06 at 38B.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Baseline InternVL3 model sizes on Q-Bench
reader_labels.reason: Reported baseline accuracy rises from 70.37 at 2B to 75.59 at 8B and 76.85 at 38B (r10–r12); this supports increasing downstream performance with model size in these tested models, not a specific fitted law.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: InternVL3-8B-Instruct fine-tuned on varying Q-Instruct ratios
reader_labels.reason: All reported ratios exceed the pretrained-model accuracy, but scores vary nonmonotonically and 20% data (78.93) exceeds full-data fine-tuning (77.73), so performance does not increase predictably with data quantity in this setting (r1–r9).
